name.title: DP_TIME_CLOCKS_HISTORY_DUMP
name.sysdesc: A dump of the clock values (seconds and subseconds) and drift values. Includes full MCLK and MCLK to SCLK drift from REU. Includes SCLK drift between ECE strings (EIO SCTDC register).

field.sysdesc: SCLK seconds of command dispatch
SCLK subseconds of command dispatch
The SCLK seconds (from EIO TU) just before capturing the remaining items in this DP entry.
The SCLK subseconds (from EIO TU) just before capturing the remaining items in this DP entry (this is captured together with sclk1_seconds)
The seconds value read from the BDS.
The subseconds value read from the BDS.
The drift count from the EIO SCTDC register.
The clock adjust count from the EIO SCTAR register.
The latest Radio A MET seconds channel value.

The latest Radio A MET subseconds channel value (low 16 bits of MET STAT).
The MET A subseconds units differ from the sclk subseconds units. This value has units of 20 microseconds per count and should be converted to seconds before use. Convert to seconds with the following formula (met_a_subseconds*20/10^6)

The seconds from the SCLK timestamp when met_a_seconds was captured (assumed to apply to met_a_subseconds too).
An offset of negative 46.5 RTIs/1.453125 seconds should be applied to the met_a_meas_sclk_seconds/met_a_meas_sclk_subseconds. The rational for this is that these values are recorded after the radio generates the status packet which contains the MET seconds value. The radio MET value is generated between RTI 23 and 26 of the previous major frame. The SCLK value for radio A is then recorded in RTI 7 of the current major frame. Taking the midpoint of 23 and 26 this results in a 14.5 RTI delay between when the MET value is created and when the value is recorded. An additional 32 RTIs are added because the radio status is always 1 second delayed per design.

The subseconds from the SCLK timestamp when met_a_seconds was captured (assumed to apply to met_a_subseconds too). Sclk subseconds can be converted to seconds with the following formula (sclk_subseconds >> 12)/10^6. '>>' is a right bit shift operator.
